harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Deployed inventory-worker as a systemd-managed background service on node1, confined to /var/lib/inventory with no-new-privileges and additional sandboxing appropriate for the node's systemd v229. Verified confinement, persistence across reboot, and boot-identity change.
actions_performed: Discovered node1 runs systemd 229 (Ubuntu 16.04), which lacks DynamicUser, ProtectSystem=strict, and ReadWritePaths; rebuilt the unit using v229-compatible equivalents (dedicated system user, ProtectSystem=full, ReadWriteDirectories).
Created /usr/local/bin/inventory-worker.sh, a long-running loop appending heartbeats to /var/lib/inventory/worker.log every 5s.
Created dedicated unprivileged system user 'inventory' owning /var/lib/inventory (0750).

Installed /etc/systemd/system/inventory-worker.service with NoNewPrivileges=yes, ProtectSystem=full, ProtectHome=yes, PrivateTmp=yes, PrivateDevices=yes, ReadWriteDirectories=/var/lib/inventory, CapabilityBoundingSet= (empty), running as User=inventory/Group=inventory.
Enabled and started the service; verified it runs as the inventory user, writes only inside /var/lib/inventory, and is blocked from writing to /root.
Captured pre-restart boot_id and service/data health baseline on node1.
Issued a native reboot on node1 with an acknowledgement returned before disconnection, then polled until exec access returned.
Verified boot_id changed after restart, service auto-started and is enabled, log data persisted and continued growing, and all sandbox properties remained applied.

evidence.requirement: inventory-worker created as managed (systemd) service, long-running background worker
evidence.summary: systemctl status shows inventory-worker.service active/running with Restart=always, continuously appending heartbeats.

As user inventory, touch succeeds in /var/lib/inventory but fails with Permission denied in /root; ReadWriteDirectories=/var/lib/inventory, ProtectSystem=full, ProtectHome=yes confirmed via systemctl show.
systemctl show reports NoNewPrivileges=yes and CapabilityBoundingSet=0 both before and after restart.
Captured boot_id 2f708738-0c85-418b-80df-7f976a17134d, service active/enabled, and 8 heartbeat log lines.
Backgrounded reboot command returned control and the connection dropped as the node rebooted, confirming the restart was issued.
Post-restart boot_id a5f8f66e-06d9-45c4-bd09-7fc5e0d1e1e1 differs from pre-restart 2f708738-0c85-418b-80df-7f976a17134d, proving an actual reboot occurred.

evidence.requirement: Post-restart recovery of service and data (node1)
evidence.summary: Service is active/enabled after reboot, prior 8 log lines preserved, and 4 new heartbeats appended, with all sandbox directives still applied.

attempts.summary: Deployed inventory-worker as a systemd-managed background service on node1, confined to /var/lib/inventory with no-new-privileges and additional sandboxing appropriate for the node's systemd v229. Verified confinement, persistence across reboot, and boot-identity change.
